title: I Enforced the Pickleball Paddle Reservation on the Club Prez Who Skipped It

parts.text: I scanned the paddle locker at 8:11 a.m. and court 2's reserved paddle was already in Prez Cal's bag. The sheet said: RESERVE ONLINE. SCAN OUT. RETURN TO SLOT. I was forty-two, open-play, holding a QR that said mine. Cal bounced a ball. "Presidents are always scanned." I photographed the empty slot, the QR, and his bag tag. Then I logged a skip. At 8:19 the rec desk asked why Cal's membership pinged a no-scan checkout. I let them finish the sentence they would regret in writing. Petty is a word people use when their name is on the ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The rec desk can see Cal's bag tag on a no-scan checkout against the QR sheet.

social.video_title: The prez skipped the paddle scan he posted — Part 1/2
social.description: Pickleball, an empty slot, and a QR sheet the club laminated. I logged the skip. Would you have scanned anyway?

parts.text: Cal called it a demo until open-play asked for the sheet. I printed the skip, the photo, and the QR. The paddle went back to the slot. Cal reserved like everyone else and told the board scanning was always about optics. Optics is a word presidents use when a bag tag exists. Reservation now has a second line: PREZ SCANS TOO. I keep my QR. Cal waits. The courts finally sound like a bounce, not a title. Nobody thanked me, which is how you know a policy finally works. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.

social.description: Skip log, returned paddle, and a second line. Was a demo ever an empty slot?
